newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. GOV SAYS TO FIGHT CLINTON'S LINE-ITEM VETO.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. GOV SAYS TO FIGHT CLINTON'S LINE-ITEM VETO.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki said Monday he would fight President Clinton's line-item veto of a provision in the balanced-budget accord giving the state favorable treatment on Medicaid costs.

"President Clinton's veto, if not overriden, is a body blow to our health care network that could endanger $2.6 billion for the health care of our children and our neediest citizens," Pataki said in a statement.
Pataki said the move punishes New York's poor, rather than the special interest groups it was designed to target.

"We will take every action necessary to defend our children and our poor families from this irresponsible decision," Pataki said. "We will fight in Congress and in the courts to deliver much needed health care services to our children and neediest citizens."

Pataki, who scheduled a press conference for 1600 EDT/2000 GMT in New York City, urged the state's Congressional delegation "to unite in a bipartisan fashion to stop President Clinton from singling out families and children for punishment."
Clinton announced earlier Monday he would use the line-item veto for the first time to strike down the New York Medicaid provision and to eliminate two tax breaks.
Clinton said the move would "ensure that national interests prevail over narrow interests."
The Medicaid provision had been expected to cost the federal government $200 million over five years.
